about: The Fasteners bridge's tools for agents (through Agent Link), listed only when Fasteners Workbench is installed: name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

fastener_types.description: Fasteners Workbench's types, sizes and lengths, from its own tables: query (words, e.g. "socket cap"), standard (ISO, DIN, ASME …), kind (screw, nut, washer, insert, pin …) list types; type gives its sizes; type and size give its lengths and holes (tap hole from its calculator; an IUT insert's hole). Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.
fastener_types.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_add.description: A Fasteners Workbench part (screw, nut, washer, insert …): type (ISO4762 …), size (M3, which wins over the hole; left out on edges: matched to the hole), length (mm, the nearest it has), thread simple|real; edges ["Plate.Edge7" or { body, near: [x,y,z] } — a point on the edge or the hole's centre] attach one to each round edge (match outer: pass hole, inner: tap hole; invert, offset mm) — a size given on a counterbore's wall goes on the bore's edge at its floor, and says so — else loose at [x,y,z]. Answers each one made: type, size, length, where, attached to (and that edge's diameter). Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer. Each attached fastener is kept on its hole by the edge's geometry too (centre, axis, radius): when a later PartDesign feature renumbers the Body's edges it is put back on the same round edge (reattached); when no edge of that size is left within reach it stays put and says so (lost, and a Report-view warning). Labels read "M8x25-Screw", "M8x25-Screw 2" …, numbered per size and kept.

edges.description: Round edges: "Plate.Edge7", or { body, near: [x, y, z] }: a point on the round edge, or the hole's centre (within 1 mm of either; at a centre, the nearest centre, then the hole's outer rim).

fastener_add.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_set.description: Change Fasteners parts in place (each keeps its object name and label) as its Change Parameters, Flip and Move do: objects, and type (one with the same properties), size ("Auto": matched to its hole), length (nearest it has), thread, invert, offset, match, edge (move it to another round edge), label (one fastener: the label it keeps; else Workshop keeps "M8x25-Screw", "M8x25-Screw 2" … numbered per size, though Fasteners relabels at every recompute). restore: true gives its objects back their behaviour in a file saved without Fasteners loaded.

label.description: One fastener's label, kept as given across recomputes (Fasteners' own relabelling is undone).

fastener_set.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_list.description: The Fasteners parts in the document (type, size, length, thread, what each is attached to) and their bill of materials, counted as Fasteners counts them (links and arrays too); sheet: true puts the BOM in a spreadsheet (its Generate BOM in the window). Each attached fastener is checked against its hole first and says hole: kept, reattached (put back on the same circle when FreeCAD renumbered the edges) or lost (its hole moved or was removed; also under warnings — fastener_set { edge } puts it on one). Fasteners from before Workshop kept them (older documents) are taken in as the document opens or recomputes: their hole from the edge they are on, a label Fasteners counted up put back in the per-size scheme; adopted: true says so.
fastener_list.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time

fastener_print.description: Fasteners' 3D-print thread settings, read; or set: mode standard|3dprint, nut [A, B] and screw [A, B] (a printed thread's diameter is d x A + B). Threaded fasteners are redone.
fastener_print.source: Workshop for FreeCAD (Fasteners bridge), calling Fasteners Workbench at run time
